title: RIP Canva? How All-in-One Design Tools Work
subtitle: Why Kittl bundles AI, templates, and mockups in one place
intro: Your reel said "Rip canva this tool does it all!!" — Kittl.com promising AI generation, templates, text effects and mockups in one tab. Why bundle everything instead of using separate apps?
takeaway: All-in-one tools like Kittl trade a little depth for a lot of speed by bundling templates, AI, and mockups together.

sections.heading: Analogy: the craft room vs. the craft cart
sections.body:
Imagine Canva as a big craft room with every tool on different tables.

Kittl is like a rolling cart that brings your favorites to you: AI image generation to create a starting picture, customizable templates to skip blank-page work, text effects to style words in one click, and mockup creation to see it on a shirt or poster.

One cart means you finish faster, which leads to why it exists.

sections.heading: Why does this exist?: speed you don't pay for twice
sections.body:
An all-in-one tool exists to remove switching. A template is a pre-made layout you edit. AI generation is typing a prompt to get an image. Mockup creation is placing your design on a product photo automatically.

Kittl bundles them so you ideate, design, and present without exporting between apps.

That speed is great until you hit its limits.

sections.heading: What can go wrong: when all-in-one means not-enough
sections.body:
What breaks first if you grow 100x?

- Templates start looking the same as everyone else's
- AI images need heavy fixing for brand details
- Advanced text effects or mockups hit paywalls or quality limits

You gain speed, you lose uniqueness and control. Use the bundle to start fast, then customize outside it when your brand needs more.

steps.narration: You start with an idea, not a blank canvas.

You drop it into a customizable template.

You publish without switching apps — until you outgrow the bundle.
